FFPO-TZ-02.model_answer: In the jungle the tiger would live freely, move through long grass and hunt animals according to his natural instincts. His strength would have a real purpose because he would be part of the wild environment. In the zoo, however, he is trapped behind bars and has very little space to move. He cannot hunt or choose where to go. His quiet pacing shows frustration and suppressed anger. The poem therefore presents captivity as a denial of the tiger's natural life. The contrast also encourages sympathy for animals kept in unnatural conditions.

FFPR2-006.model_answer: Hunger helps the young seagull overcome his fear because his desire for food becomes stronger than his fear of flying. He has been sitting alone on the ledge while his brothers and sister have already learnt to fly. His parents refuse to bring him food while he remains afraid. His mother finally comes near him carrying a piece of fish. When he sees the food, he jumps towards it without thinking about his fear. During the jump he spreads his wings and discovers that he can fly. The experience gives him confidence and helps him become independent.

FFPR2-010.model_answer: Anne's attitude towards writing changes as she continues to keep her diary. At first she sees the diary mainly as a private friend to whom she can confide her thoughts. Gradually, writing becomes a serious means of examining her feelings, experiences and relationships. She learns to express ideas more clearly and honestly through her entries. Her writing also becomes more thoughtful and reflective as she grows. She begins to understand that writing can help her organise confusing emotions. Thus the diary develops from a simple confidant into an important form of self-expression.

FFPR2-012.model_answer: Coorg is described as a place of natural beauty and adventure because it has green hills, forests, coffee plantations and pleasant scenery. The region is rich in wildlife and offers opportunities for outdoor activities. Visitors can enjoy trekking, rafting and other adventurous experiences. The landscape combines natural beauty with a strong local culture and traditions. The people of Coorg are also described as brave and hospitable. The variety of scenery and activities makes the region attractive to travellers. Thus Coorg offers both peaceful natural surroundings and exciting adventures.

FFPR2-017.model_answer: Kisa Gotami learns from Buddha that death is a universal truth that no family can escape. She first approaches him in deep grief and hopes that he can restore her dead son. Buddha asks her to collect mustard seeds from a house where no one has died. Her search leads her from one home to another, but she finds that every family has experienced death. She gradually understands that her suffering is part of a universal human experience. This realisation helps her accept her son's death. She learns that wisdom and peace come from accepting the natural order of life.

FFPR2-019.model_answer: The arguments about Oxen Meadows and Guess become comic because they are completely out of proportion to the serious purpose of Lomov's visit. Lomov comes to propose to Natalya, but their conversation quickly turns into a quarrel about property. They then argue about which dog is better. Natalya and Chubukov become as heated as Lomov over these trivial matters. The characters use insulting and exaggerated language while discussing subjects that should be minor. Their stubbornness makes the proposal almost disappear from the conversation. This contrast between marriage and constant quarrelling creates much of the play's humour.

FP-BH-02.model_answer: Education transforms Bholi by giving her confidence, self-respect and the ability to speak for herself. At first she is neglected by her family and is afraid because people make fun of her speech and appearance. Her teacher treats her kindly and encourages her to learn without fear. School gradually improves Bholi's language and confidence. She begins to understand that she deserves respect and need not accept humiliation. This new self-confidence enables her to reject Bishamber when he demands dowry and insults her. Education therefore changes Bholi from a timid girl into an independent and courageous young woman.

FP-MS-02.model_answer: Richard Ebright became a successful scientist through curiosity, hard work and disciplined study. His mother encouraged him to read, observe nature and take part in scientific activities. His interest in butterflies developed from collecting them into careful scientific investigation. He learnt to ask questions and conduct experiments instead of remaining satisfied with simple observation. His competitive spirit and determination also helped him improve his work. These qualities together supported his development as a successful scientist.

FP-NK-01.model_answer: The necklace changes Matilda and her husband's lives by turning a desire for social appearance into years of hardship. Matilda borrows the necklace because she wants to look wealthy and elegant at the ball. When it is lost, the couple borrow money to buy a replacement. They spend many years working and living in poverty to repay their debts. Matilda's appearance and circumstances change completely during this period. Later she discovers that the original necklace was only an imitation and was worth very little. The revelation shows how the desire to appear rich brought unnecessary suffering.

FWF2-007.model_answer: The ending of 'The Necklace' creates irony because Matilda spends ten years repaying the cost of a replacement necklace that was not actually necessary. She and her husband believe the original necklace is valuable and sacrifice their comfortable life to replace it. Matilda becomes poor and aged through years of hard work. When she finally tells Madame Forestier what happened, she learns that the borrowed necklace was an imitation. The truth is completely opposite to what Matilda had believed. This unexpected revelation makes the ending both tragic and ironic. It also reinforces the danger of judging happiness and value by outward appearance.
